articles.title: Stark warning – does new footage in Avengers: Endgame reveal the truth about Doctor Doom?
articles.summary: Warning: contains spoilers The four short scenes added to the new version has made the film the highest-grossing of all time – but the only people really enjoying this are the Disney accountants. Does it really matter which film is the highest-grossing of all time at the global box office?
body: And yet the most interesting thing about Avengers: Endgame’s return to cinemas is not how much money it has made – for the record, the rerelease, titled Avengers Endgame: Encore, had brought in another $126m worldwide by last weekend, taking its lifetime total to approximately $2.925bn (just ahead of Avatar’s $2.923bn) – but what Marvel added to the picture while we were all busy counting.

Premium-format presentations of the new version feature a new scene at the end of the film and another three during and after its credits, with some also appearing in standard screenings. The idea is presumably that these tantalising snippets will segue viewers smoothly into the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday with the sort of spring in the step that can only come from being convinced that they are now three tiny clues away from understanding the mind of Kevin Feige.

articles.title: Tenzing review – reconstruction of first summit of Everest puts Sherpa at the centre of the story
articles.summary: Genden Phuntsok brings charm and innocence to his portrayal of Tenzing Norgay, while Tom Hiddleston is suitably frank as Edmund Hillary. Here is a well intentioned, watchable, if sometimes soft-edged film with some NatGeo production values and greenscreen jeopardy on high mountain peaks.
body: Tenzing, a former Sherpa guide whose unparalleled knowledge of the mountain and exemplary climbing skills earned him promotion to full team member, is played here by Tibetan actor Genden Phuntsok, while Hillary is robustly portrayed by Tom Hiddleston. Screenwriter Luke Davies and director Jennifer Peedom have the decent aim of restoring Tenzing’s achievement to the centre of the narrative, a tale which at the time was resoundingly claimed for Hillary and the British empire: a glorious redemption of Scott’s Antarctic ordeal 41 years earlier and a sign of divine approval for the imminent coronation of Queen Elizabeth II.

articles.title: DC Comics Now Sits Within Skydance Products & Publishing Division, Alongside Warner Bros. and Paramount Consumer Products Groups
articles.summary: The new Skydance, formed from the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, has consolidated its publishing and consumer-products teams into one group — Skydance Products & Publishing — led by Josh Silverman.
body: DC Comics will come under Silverman’s leadership alongside Paramount Global Publishing, Paramount and WBD licensed publishing, WBD consumer products and Paramount consumer products, as well as brand partnerships, retail and e-commerce, and other commercial initiatives across the company’s portfolio of brands.

Skydance Products & Publishing, working with the company’s TV and film divisions, is responsible for managing licensing for brands and franchises including Harry Potter, Game of Thrones, The Lord of the Rings, DC, Star Trek, SpongeBob SquarePants, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Hanna-Barbera and Looney Tunes, among others.

Prior to joining Paramount last year, Silverman was chief franchise officer of Mattel, where he expanded the company’s global consumer products and publishing businesses and oversaw more than 165 consumer product partnerships tied to the “Barbie” movie. He also has held senior leadership roles at Disney, including as EVP of global third-party commercialization leading consumer product licensing, and Marvel Entertainment.

articles.title: Lost generation: the AI threat to Britain’s next great directors
articles.summary: Commercials once launched careers from Ridley Scott to Guy Ritchie, now automated production is cutting costs – and the chance to learn by doing. When Ridley Scott was awarded the UK’s highest accolade for a glittering career directing films from Alien and Blade Runner to Gladiator and The Martian…
body: The advertising industry has long been a breeding ground for British film and TV talent who have gone on to make the jump to Hollywood productions, including Guy Ritchie, who started out making music videos and commercials, and Paddington in Peru director Dougal Wilson, whose credits include a number of John Lewis’s famous Christmas ads.

But the panicked race to introduce AI technology across the advertising industry, to cut client costs and avoid being pushed aside by big tech, has raised fears of a lost generation who may be denied the opportunity to develop into great British film and TV directors.
“100%, yes, I have fears,” says Luke Scott, who runs the group that includes Ridley Scott Associates, the media production company that was co-founded by his father in the 1960s.

“I’m grown up enough to recognise that change is inevitable. But what I’ve seen generally in terms of generative AI output is a very mixed bag. You can turn to it and do something and say ‘Look what I made and isn’t it edifying’. But that is very misleading and sort of introducing us to an ersatz creativity.
points: Commercials once launched careers from Ridley Scott to Guy Ritchie, now automated production is cutting costs – and the chance to learn by doing.

articles.title: Lightsaber Darth Vader used in ‘I am your father’ Star Wars duel up for auction
articles.summary: Saber is expected to fetch at least $1m and is one of more than two dozen props that will be up for sale. A lightsaber used by Darth Vader in the Star Wars duel where he tells Luke Skywalker “I am your father” is going up for sale at Heritage Auctions next month.
body: The Vader saber, also used in Return of the Jedi, is expected to fetch at least $1m. It is one of more than two dozen lightsaber props that will be up for sale at the auction that spans Star Wars Episodes I through IX and other films and TV shows from the universe George Lucas created.
Others include dueling lightsabers wielded by Ewan McGregor’s Obi-Wan Kenobi and Hayden Christensen’s Anakin Skywalker in Revenge of the Sith that are expected to go for at least $10,000 apiece.

In July, a lightsaber with Luke Skywalker’s severed hand from The Empire Strikes Back sold for $3.75m at auction, the highest price ever fetched for a prop used in a Star Wars film according to the auction house.
An EE-3 carbine blaster wielded by Boba Fett throughout The Empire Strikes Back is estimated to bring in more than $100,000.

articles.title: ‘Mystery Science Theater 3000: The RiffTrax Experiments’: Behind the Scenes of the Satellite of Love
articles.summary: In a cozy suburb of Minneapolis, a guy in a blue jumpsuit is once again stuck aboard a space station with his robot pals, watching the worst movies ever made. To paraphrase the show’s catchy theme song, if you’re wondering how that works, it’s just a TV show, so you should really just relax. In
body: Joel Hodgson created and starred as that guy forced to screen cheesy flicks; he left mid-run and was replaced by Michael J. Nelson. After the show wrapped, Nelson and fellow “MST3K” writer-stars Kevin Murphy and Bill Corbett took the basic idea and launched their own version, RiffTrax, which started as a website and branched out into live performances and its own FAST channel.
Then, in 2017, Hodgson revived “MST3K” at Netflix and launched a related streaming platform called The Gizmoplex, but the RiffTrax team wasn’t involved.

That all changed this year. In January, Hodgson sold his ownership in the series to Radial Entertainment and once again departed. Radial then recruited the RiffTrax team to return for four new episodes. “Mystery Science Theater 3000: The RiffTrax Experiments” was born.

The transition of “MST3K” to Radial allowed the company to approach the RiffTrax team (who hadn’t been formally involved in any new interations of the show since 1999) about joining forces, which they were eager to do. Fans were in: They raised $2.7 million in a Kickstarter campaign to fund the revival, and “The RiffTrax Experiments” were off and running.

articles.title: Jeissy Trompiz’s ‘Three Houses’ Explores a Venezuela Where Afro and Indigenous Communities Sit on the ‘Periphery of the Periphery’
articles.summary: “I don’t know what to tell you.” For a time, that was Jeissy Trompiz’s answer when his Brazilian filmmaker friend would ask him about Venezuela. Trompiz left Maracaibo, the oil city where he grew up, in 2014 to study filmmaking at the International School of Film and TV in Cuba, just before…
body: When he finally returned home, he was confronted with a changed country he had struggled to explain — even to himself.
“The situation was really sad and shocking,” he told Variety. He couldn’t shake the comparison to Cuba, another country in crisis.
“When I went back to Venezuela, I started to think: Now I can tell you.”
So he started filming “Three Houses” (“Tres casas”), a documentary that takes the form of a video letter from Maracaibo to his friend. Trompiz describes making it as a form of “therapy.”

articles.title: ‘Helluva Boss’ Actor Lashes Out at NYCC Heckler: ‘I’m Going to Jump Over This Fence and End You’
articles.summary: It was a “helluva” time at New York City Comic-Con, where an audience remember interrupted the “Helluva Boss” panel by repeatedly shouting over the cast. Following multiple attempts to silence the heckling, actor Brandon Rogers seemingly threatened the fan in a video posted online.
body: When nobody on the NYCC staff stepped in, Rogers asked, “Isn’t there someone in a vest? Bulletproof one, maybe?” After a bit of silence, he added, “Is anyone working this fucking event? Can someone please get this motherfucker the hell out of here? I swear to God.”

In a statement to Variety, a spokesperson for ReedPop wrote, “We are aware of a repeated disturbance from a fan in the audience during Thursday’s ‘Helluva Boss’ panel. While the situation was addressed after the panel, action was not taken swiftly enough, and we apologize to the panelists, moderator, and fans in attendance for the disruption. We are taking steps to ensure any future incidents are addressed in a swifter manner.”

The panel also featured Vivian Nichole Nixon, Erica Lindbeck, Bryce Pinkham, Harvey Guillén, Vivienne Medrano, Richard Steven Horvitz and Perri Nemiroff to discuss the animated series, which Rogers wrote and developed.

articles.title: Two Renoir paintings stolen from French museum are recovered
articles.summary: The two works were seized last month when thieves cut through a fence and smashed a window at the Renoir Museum on the French Riviera.
body: Two paintings by Auguste Renoir stolen a month ago from a museum in the south of France have been recovered, the local town hall has said.
The two works were seized on 8 September when thieves cut through a fence and smashed a window at the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer, where the French impressionist had lived during his final years.
The local mayor praised authorities for recovering the paintings and said the news gave immense joy and profound relief.
Six suspects have also been arrested in relation with the heist at Renoir Museum, the town hall confirmed in a statement.

articles.summary: During a London Film Festival chat, the filmmaker also recalled his “uneventful” meeting with Rupert Murdoch after his ‘Slumdog Millionaire’ made the mogul’s studio “a lot of money.”
body: Director and producer Danny Boyle discussed his latest film, Ink, which traces Rupert Murdoch ‘s rise on Fleet Street and takeover of the tabloid The Sun, and his film career at an event during the 70th edition of the BFI London Film Festival on Friday. And he shared some thoughts that surprised audience members.
The filmmaker talked to Puck ‘s Matt Belloni in a wide-ranging discussion that was partially recorded for his The Town podcast.

Boyle recalled an encounter with Murdoch. “I met him, not for this project, but because Slumdog Millionaire … made him a lot of money,” he said. “[Fox Searchlight] were the studio that picked it up and made a huge amount of money,” so Boyle was invited to “a lunch party in a garden somewhere.” But he acknowledged: “I can’t remember [details], and it was an extremely uneventful meeting.” Related Stories.
